title: Northgate Optical Accidental Damage Coverage: Start of the Replacement Clock
content:
For an accidental damage replacement of Northgate Optical eyewear, the replacement clock runs from a clock start to the day the replacement is authorized. A remake already on the job moves the clock start as follows.

**Interpretation.** Where a prescription-change remake stands on the job, the replacement clock start is the opening date of the latest prescription-change remake; where none stands but a non-adapt remake stands, the replacement clock start is the opening date of the latest non-adapt remake. Where the job carries neither, this interpretation sets no clock start.

**Records read.** A remake "stands" on the job when the job carries a remake charge entry with that remake reason. Its opening date is the date of that entry, and the latest is the one with the latest date. Remakes for other reasons — lab defect, frame defect, accidental damage — do not move the clock start under this interpretation.

## Combinations

| Prescription-change remake on the job | Non-adapt remake on the job | Replacement clock start |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | opening date of the latest prescription-change remake |
| yes | no | opening date of the latest prescription-change remake |
| no | yes | opening date of the latest non-adapt remake |
| no | no | not set by this interpretation |

## Illustrations (hypothetical jobs)

- A job with a non-adapt remake opened on 3 March and a prescription-change remake opened on 20 February of the same year: the prescription-change remake governs, so the clock starts on 20 February, even though the non-adapt remake is later.
- A job with two non-adapt remakes, opened on 5 April and 18 June, and no prescription-change remake: the clock starts on 18 June.
